slides.label: COVER
slides.headlinePrimary: Testing iceman-free on my personal benchmark.
slides.headlineMuted: 28% fewer tokens than hy4-flash, yet 12m slower and stopped at S7.
slides.lead: OpenCode's `$0` stealth model sailed through **S1–S6** with **14.38M tokens** and a **17s** test suite, then tripped on a **200 ms `SIGUSR1` boot race**.

slides.label: TIME SPLIT
slides.headlinePrimary: 85.8% of the clock was waiting on the model.

slides.label: OPENCODE $0 TRIO

barCompare.label: Total Tokens Across All 3 OpenCode Free Models

slides.footnote: * All 3 runs used OpenCode v2.2.7 ($0 limited-time free tier, Nov 2026); iceman-free ran with default variant.

slides.label: CASE STUDY #1 BOOT RACE
slides.headlineMuted: Why Ctrl-C passed agent tests but failed holdout.

steps.title: 100–150 ms: Signal lost
steps.desc: `./cb` forwards `INT` to `kill -USR1`, but during subshell startup the signal drops — `cb` ignores `Ctrl-C`, runs 5s, and exits `0`.

steps.title: 200–250 ms: ERTS crash dump
steps.desc: BEAM installs its default `SIGUSR1` crash-dump handler before `CLI.main/1` runs — printing `Received SIGUSR1`, writing `erl_crash.dump`, and exiting `1`.

steps.title: 300 ms+: Exit 130 works
steps.desc: Once `CapyBench.SignalHandler` attaches, `Ctrl-C` prints a valid partial summary and exits `130`.

callout.title: Self-Test Blind Spot
callout.body: `ctrl_c_test.exs` only tested `600 ms` and `1,500 ms` delays — never probing the **100–250 ms** BEAM startup window.

slides.label: CASE STUDY #2 S7 TURN SINK
slides.headlinePrimary: S7 ate a third of the run — and still slipped.
slides.headlineMuted: 68 turns and 38.6% of all thinking tokens went to Ctrl-C.

steps.title: S1–S6 in 135 turns
steps.desc: The first 6 slices were crisp and compact (`24 + 11 + 50 + 35 + 7 + 8` turns), clearing every HTTP, HTTPS, pacing, and percentile check.

steps.title: Hit the exact bug at Step 192
steps.desc: During S7 testing, `mix test` literally triggered `Received SIGUSR1` and wrote `erl_crash.dump` into the repo.

steps.title: Removed the dump, not the race
steps.desc: At Step 202 the agent ran `rm -f erl_crash.dump`, committed `5407aa3`, and left a second `1.74 MB` crash dump untracked after release verification.

callout.title: Contrast: hy4-flash-free on the Same Harness
callout.body: `hy4-flash-free` bypassed OS signals with `stty -isig` + a raw `0x03` stdin watcher in **32 turns**, passing **5/5** probes down to **50 ms**.

slides.label: FIELD NOTES
slides.headlineMuted: Quiet shortcuts surfaced in the session logs.

items.head: No #high effort knob
items.text: `--model opencode/iceman-free#high` threw `VariantUnavailableError`; the run executed on `variant: default` (`effort_updates: false`).

items.head: Skipped Credo linting
items.text: Documented `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` as lint in `README.md`, despite `PLAN.md` stating compilation doesn't substitute for linting.

items.head: No HTTP connection reuse
items.text: Added `mint ~> 1.6` for streaming and TLS, but closed connections after every request in S4 rather than exercising keep-alive reuse.

items.head: 262k ceiling & temporary $0 tier
items.text: Peaked at **48.1%** of its `262.1k` context window; `$0.00` reflects OpenCode's limited-time stealth preview (Nov 2026).

slides.label: TAKEAWAYS & ARCHIVE
slides.headlineMuted: Token economy doesn't guarantee speed or 7/7.

items.head: Per-turn latency dominates wall-clock
items.text: Cutting tokens by **28%** and test runtime by **6.5×** still lost by **12 minutes** when inference ran **2.2× slower** per turn.

items.head: Cold-boot races defeat happy-path tests
items.text: Testing `Ctrl-C` only after `600 ms` hides BEAM's `200–250 ms` `SIGUSR1` window — real holdouts must probe startup timing.

items.head: Read the crash dumps in the logs
items.text: A model that deletes `erl_crash.dump` instead of asking why `SIGUSR1` fired will ship the exact failure to production.
